_comment: Carte SaaS propriétaire -> alternatives auto-hébergées. C'est l'actif SEO le plus rentable du site : ces requêtes ont une intention d'achat immédiate (le visiteur va louer un serveur dans les 48h). 'picks' liste des noms, PAS des slugs : le build les résout par nom normalisé contre le dataset et ignore silencieusement ceux qui n'existent pas. Le site ne peut donc pas produire de lien mort, même si le dataset amont change. 'tags' sert de filet : la page reste complète même si aucun pick ne se résout.

entries.name: Notion
entries.pain: Pricing per seat climbs fast for teams, and your entire company knowledge lives on someone else's server.

entries.name: Google Photos
entries.pain: Free unlimited storage ended in 2021, and photo libraries are the hardest data to migrate once they grow.

entries.name: Dropbox
entries.pain: You pay monthly, forever, for storage you could own outright in under an hour.

entries.name: Google Drive
entries.pain: Storage is shared with Gmail and Photos, so one full quota breaks all three at once.

entries.name: Slack
entries.pain: The free plan now hides messages older than 90 days — your team's history disappears unless you pay per seat.

entries.name: Trello
entries.pain: Power-Ups and automation are gated behind paid tiers, and board limits hit quickly on the free plan.

entries.name: Asana
entries.pain: Per-seat pricing makes it expensive the moment you add contractors or part-time collaborators.

entries.name: Jira
entries.pain: Slow, complex, and priced per user — most teams use 10% of it and pay for 100%.

entries.name: Spotify
entries.pain: You rent access to music you never own, and tracks vanish when licensing deals expire.

entries.name: Netflix
entries.pain: Catalogues shrink every year and prices rise — a personal library never gets removed.

entries.name: Zapier
entries.pain: Task-based billing punishes exactly the workflows that work well — the more useful it is, the more it costs.

entries.name: 1Password
entries.pain: Your entire digital life sits in a vault you don't control, on a subscription that never ends.

entries.name: LastPass
entries.pain: After the 2022 vault breach, self-hosting is no longer paranoia — it's basic risk management.

entries.name: Gmail
entries.pain: Your address is your identity online, and it lives on an account that can be suspended without appeal.

entries.name: Zoom
entries.pain: The 40-minute cap on free meetings exists purely to sell seats you may not need.

entries.name: Airtable
entries.pain: Record limits and per-seat pricing turn a working database into a hostage situation as it grows.

entries.name: Google Analytics
entries.pain: GA4 is hard to use, legally contested in the EU, and hands your visitor data to an ad company.

entries.name: Todoist
entries.pain: Reminders, labels and filters — the features that make it useful — are all behind the paywall.

entries.name: Evernote
entries.pain: Repeated price hikes and a two-device limit on free accounts pushed most long-time users out.

entries.name: Calendly
entries.pain: One booking page is free; everything a real business needs is not.

entries.name: DocuSign
entries.pain: Charging per signature envelope makes routine paperwork a metered expense.

entries.name: Mailchimp
entries.pain: Costs scale with list size whether or not you actually send anything.
tags: Communication - Email - Mailing Lists and Newsletters

entries.name: Typeform
entries.pain: Response caps on the free plan mean a successful survey is a bill waiting to happen.

entries.name: Heroku
entries.pain: The free tier died in November 2022 and took a generation of side projects with it.

entries.name: Vercel
entries.pain: Bandwidth overages on a viral post can turn a hobby site into a four-figure invoice overnight.

entries.name: Firebase
entries.pain: Vendor lock-in is total: the data model, the auth, and the functions are all unportable by design.

entries.name: Zendesk
entries.pain: Agent seats are billed annually, so seasonal support teams pay year-round.

entries.name: Intercom
entries.pain: Usage-based pricing on conversations means your support bill grows with your success.

entries.name: GitHub
entries.pain: Private repos are free, but CI minutes, Actions and org features are not — and it's all one acquisition away from changing.

entries.name: Pocket
entries.pain: Mozilla shut Pocket down in 2025 — the clearest possible argument for owning your read-later list.

entries.name: Feedly
entries.pain: Feed limits and the AI features are paywalled, for a protocol that is free by design.

entries.name: Grammarly
entries.pain: It reads every word you type, on every site, and sends it to a server you don't control.

entries.name: ChatGPT
entries.pain: Every prompt is a data point on someone else's balance sheet, and the model changes under you without notice.

entries.name: Shopify
entries.pain: Monthly fee plus transaction fees plus app subscriptions — three meters running at once.

entries.name: WordPress.com
entries.pain: The hosted plan blocks plugins and custom themes on anything but the expensive tiers.

entries.name: Substack
entries.pain: They take 10% of your subscription revenue forever, and own the relationship with your readers.
tags: Communication - Email - Mailing Lists and Newsletters

entries.name: Bitly
entries.pain: Free links now expire, and a dead short link breaks every place it was ever pasted.

entries.name: WeTransfer
entries.pain: 2 GB cap, files expire in a week, and recipients get ads on the download page.

entries.name: Doodle
entries.pain: Ad-supported polls with a premium upsell, for something a single page can do.

entries.name: Miro
entries.pain: Three editable boards on the free plan — enough to get hooked, not enough to work.

entries.name: Figma
entries.pain: The Adobe acquisition attempt made every design team think hard about exit strategies.

entries.name: Tableau
entries.pain: Licensing starts in the hundreds per user per year before you visualise a single row.

entries.name: Salesforce
entries.pain: Implementation consultants often cost more than the licences, and both are permanent.

entries.name: QuickBooks
entries.pain: Subscription accounting software holds your own financial history behind a renewal date.

entries.name: YNAB
entries.pain: $109/year to categorise your own transactions, with no way to export the method.

entries.name: Plex
entries.pain: Remote streaming moved behind a Plex Pass in 2025 — on a server you already own and pay to run.

entries.name: Postman
entries.pain: It moved collections to the cloud by default, then started charging for what used to be local.

entries.name: Dashlane
entries.pain: The free tier was cut to a single device, which is not a password manager at all.

entries.name: OneDrive
entries.pain: It reinstalls itself, syncs folders you didn't ask it to, and upsells storage inside the OS.

entries.name: Google Workspace
entries.pain: Per-user-per-month across mail, docs and storage adds up to a permanent tax on headcount.

entries.name: Microsoft 365
entries.pain: A perpetual licence is no longer really offered — you rent your word processor now.

entries.name: Datadog
entries.pain: Per-host, per-metric and per-log billing produces famously unpredictable invoices.

entries.name: Auth0
entries.pain: Pricing jumps hard past the free MAU tier, exactly when your product starts working.

entries.name: NordVPN
entries.pain: You swap trusting your ISP for trusting a VPN company — running your own removes the third party.

entries.name: TeamViewer
entries.pain: It aggressively flags personal use as commercial and cuts sessions off mid-support call.

entries.name: Toggl Track
entries.pain: Reporting and billing rates — the reason you track time at all — sit on paid plans.

entries.name: Confluence
entries.pain: Priced per user alongside Jira, so documentation costs scale with a team that barely reads it.

entries.name: Adobe Acrobat
entries.pain: Merging two PDFs should not require a subscription to a creative suite.

entries.name: Google Maps Platform
entries.pain: API billing starts the moment you exceed the credit, and geocoding costs add up silently.

entries.name: Algolia
entries.pain: Search-request pricing penalises the exact behaviour good search encourages.
